instruction.text: Decide whether the statement is true or false.

atoms.a: Ableism describes the discrimination of disabled individuals.
People in powerful positions, like doctors, judges, police officers and teachers can be prejudiced and use their power to harm minorities.
Identity politics serve to support minority groups in order to fight the inequalities they experience.
Different identities can overlap in one person and shape their lived experience in diverse ways.
The concept of intersectionality helps not to forget the bigger picture and take intersecting forms of identity into account.
Ongoing discrimination against marginalised people and addressing the specific needs of minorities are both arguments for identity politics.
Identities can also have positive meaning for many and foster solidarity.
Racism is barely an issue since the Civil Rights Movement.

wrong.text: While the civil rights movement ended social and legal segregation in the US, racism still persists and leads to inequality for many people of colour not just in the US.

atoms.a: The UK Equality Act 2010 only serves to protect disabled individuals.

wrong.text: The Equality Act 2010 serves to protect all marginalised minorities in the UK.

atoms.a: To create true social equality everyone has to be treated in the same way.

wrong.text: If this were true, this would only benefit the majority and the minorities interests and needs would be ignored. Equality means all people deserve dignity but not that all people are the same.

atoms.a: A prejudice can sometimes be based on truth.

wrong.text: Prejudices are social projections onto individuals or groups and are based on false understanding, missing knowledge or deliberate hate.

atoms.a: Two people who belong to the same identity group will always be treated equally.

wrong.text: Individuals often align with more than one identity group. Thus, they are not always treated the same.
